clue.text: Crazy headgear for a reckless character

parts.note: mad is a plain synonym of crazy
a cap is a simple item of headgear

explanation.surface: Someone wearing a ridiculous hat is labelled a wild, impulsive sort.
explanation.definitionFit: A madcap is a noun for an impulsive person who acts without thinking about the consequences.

clue.text: Resting place for characters in smart set

indicators.note: taking the letters that make up a phrase and using them in a fresh order

parts.note: the letters of both words together

explanation.surface: Fashionable society people look for somewhere to relax.
explanation.definitionFit: A mattress is the padded part of a bed where one lies down to sleep.

clue.text: Craved, in a way to get cut up

indicators.note: a word put another way has its letters rearranged

parts.note: the word itself, taken letter by letter

explanation.surface: Someone longed in a way to be upset or hurt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut up' also means distressed, which fits the surface; here it means sliced.
explanation.definitionFit: Carved means sliced into pieces, as a joint of meat is cut up at the table.

clue.text: Stand for friend getting round a kind of steed

indicators.note: a kind of something is a variant of it, so the letters are rearranged
the friend goes round the other part, enclosing it

parts.note: a pal is a friend
these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Holding up a friend who rides round on a particular breed of horse.
explanation.walkthrough: The friend splits around the rearranged horse: P, then the jumble, then AL.
explanation.definitionFit: A pedestal is a base or support on which a statue or column stands.

clue.text: New thought from confused aide

indicators.note: something confused is muddled, so its letters come in a scrambled order

parts.note: the word itself, taken letter by letter

explanation.surface: A muddled assistant suddenly comes up with a fresh notion.
explanation.definitionFit: An idea is a thought or notion, and a new one is exactly what the word suggests.

clue.text: Becomes as one when University briefly has set-back

indicators.note: briefly means in shortened form, so the word is cut down

parts.note: uni is the everyday short form of university

indicators.note: back attached to the word means it is read from the end

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A university suffers a setback and its staff pull together.
explanation.definitionFit: To unite is to join together into a single whole, so unites means becomes one.

clue.text: Restore losses from upset pin-less porcupine

indicators.note: something upset is knocked over and disordered, so its letters are rearranged
less attached to pin means those three letters are taken away

parts.note: the animal's name, before letters are removed

explanation.surface: An agitated porcupine that has lost its quills tries to make good what it lost.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove P, I and N from the animal to leave ORCUPE, then rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: To recoup is to recover money or ground that has been lost, making good the losses.

clue.text: Put at risk, but conclude with great displeasure

parts.note: to end something is to conclude it
anger is strong displeasure

explanation.surface: Someone takes a risk and the episode finishes with a lot of bad feeling.
explanation.definitionFit: To endanger is to expose something to harm, a verb synonym for placing it in jeopardy.

clue.text: In rows to make neckwear crimson

parts.note: a tie is worn round the neck
crimson is a shade of red

explanation.surface: A tailor lines up rows of ties to produce something deep red.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiered seating or a tiered cake is arranged in rising layers, one row above another.

clue.text: Formerly with Canberra I get on to produce extortion

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife
Canberra lies in the ACT, the Australian Capital Territory
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Canberra resident from the past seems to be running a shakedown racket.
explanation.walkthrough: This is a Canberra Times puzzle, so the capital stands for its territory's abbreviation, ACT.
explanation.definitionFit: Exaction is the demanding of money by force or authority, so it is a close synonym for extortion.

clue.text: Treasure Island writer involves first lady in high jinks

indicators.note: to involve is to take in or include, so one part is wrapped around the other

parts.note: the initials of Robert Louis Stevenson, author of Treasure Island
Eve is the first woman in the Bible

explanation.surface: An author is pictured putting a famous woman into a story of riotous fun.
explanation.walkthrough: The author is reduced to his initials, which then wrap around the biblical first woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Revels are lively, noisy celebrations, which is the boisterous merriment that high jinks describes.

clue.text: Patterns forming an arm of the church

indicators.note: the letters are being shaped into something new, so they must be rearranged

parts.note: the word itself, taken letter by letter

explanation.surface: Decorative designs make up part of a church building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Patterns' looks like the definition, but it is only the letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A transept is either of the two side wings crossing the nave of a cross-shaped church building.

clue.text: Overbearing, but arrive briefly and tango wildly

indicators.note: briefly means in shortened form, so the word is cut down

parts.note: the word before shortening; arr. is its timetable abbreviation

indicators.note: a dance done wildly has its steps thrown about, so the letters scatter

parts.note: the word itself, taken letter by letter

explanation.surface: A haughty dancer turns up and dances a frenzied tango.
explanation.walkthrough: ARR is the abbreviation for arrive used on timetables.
explanation.definitionFit: Arrogant means having an exaggerated sense of one's own importance, which is how an overbearing person acts.

clue.text: Listener with doctor in the summit shows sign of sorrow

indicators.note: the listener and doctor are put inside the summit, enclosed by it

parts.note: the top is the summit
the ear is the organ that listens
Dr is the abbreviation for doctor

explanation.surface: A mountaineer and a doctor at the peak are pictured looking sad.
explanation.definitionFit: A teardrop is a single tear, a visible token of grief or unhappiness.

clue.text: Short way to a big wave for a small pram

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for Street, a way
a roller is a long, heavy wave

explanation.surface: A short route to the surf is found for a baby carriage.
explanation.definitionFit: A stroller is a light pushchair, a smaller and more folding kind of baby carriage than a full pram.

clue.text: Binds about 499 or 501 and neatens

indicators.note: one word goes about another, surrounding it

parts.note: to tie is to bind
in Roman numerals ID is 499 and DI is 501; either fits inside

explanation.surface: Someone ties up a bundle of roughly five hundred items to tidy it.
explanation.walkthrough: Inserting ID after T, or DI after TI, gives the same letters, so the setter offers both numbers. The paper prints '50', most likely a lost digit, since 50 (L) fits nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: To tidy is to put in order, so tidies means makes neat.

clue.text: Bull-ring cheers about four fruits

indicators.note: the cheers go about the number, surrounding it

parts.note: ole is the shout of approval at a bullfight
IV is four in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Spectators at a bullfight shout over a handful of pieces of fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: Olives are the small oily fruits of the olive tree, so they are an example of fruits.

clue.text: She, sir, might become a maker of disapproving noises

indicators.note: becoming something else means changing form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters of both words together

explanation.surface: A man is warned that a woman could turn into someone who heckles.
explanation.definitionFit: A hisser makes the sharp hissing noise that audiences use to show disapproval.

clue.text: Twist or Hardy — alternative to dwell in

indicators.note: the dwelling word goes in, placed inside the alternative word

parts.note: or is the word that offers an alternative
to live somewhere is to dwell there

explanation.surface: A quiz-like pairing of two famous names, followed by talk of another place to live.
explanation.walkthrough: Oliver Twist is Dickens's orphan; Oliver Hardy is the comedian of Laurel and Hardy. The second word goes inside the first.
explanation.definitionFit: Both figures share the first name Oliver, so either one defines the answer by example.

clue.text: After the year 1001 make a phone call — showing kind feelings

indicators.note: the phone call is to be placed following the dated year, setting the order of the parts

parts.note: AD, anno domini, marks a year of the Christian era
M is 1000 and I is 1 in Roman numerals
to ring someone is to phone them

explanation.surface: A historical date is followed by someone picking up the telephone warmly.
explanation.walkthrough: The date reads as AD 1001 in Roman form, and the call is added after it.
explanation.definitionFit: Admiring means regarding with approval and warm respect, a participle matching showing kind feelings.

clue.text: Flower, initially, is red in spring

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of each word that follows

parts.note: the opening letters of these four words

explanation.surface: A flower shows red colour at the start of the season.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Initially' seems to modify the flower; it applies to the four words after it.
explanation.definitionFit: The iris is a garden flower with sword-shaped leaves, many kinds of which bloom in spring.

clue.text: Reply to a New South Wales verbal delay

parts.note: taken as written
the standard abbreviation of the Australian state
er is the hesitating sound a speaker makes

explanation.surface: Responding to a hesitant voice from Sydney's state.
explanation.definitionFit: An answer is a reply, the noun for something said or written in response.

clue.text: Obliteration for confused teen-idol

indicators.note: something confused is mixed up, so its letters come out in a jumbled order

parts.note: the letters of both words together

explanation.surface: A bewildered pop star faces being wiped from fans' memories.
explanation.definitionFit: A deletion is a wiping out or removal, the same sense as obliteration.

clue.text: Vase in the garbage dump produces this vegetable

indicators.note: the vase is placed inside the dump, so one set of letters sits within the other

parts.note: a tip is a rubbish dump
an urn is a kind of vase

explanation.surface: Someone finds a pot at the rubbish tip, and something edible comes out of it.
explanation.walkthrough: A tip is the British and Australian word for a rubbish dump.
explanation.definitionFit: A turnip is a root crop eaten as a vegetable, so it is an example of the category.
